merger_description:
Funds managed and/or advised by Bain Capital Investors, LLC (together, **Bain Capital**) propose to acquire 51% of the shares and voting rights in Everllence SE (**Everllence**) and a number of its direct and indirect subsidiaries (together, the **Everllence Group**) from Volkswagen Vermögensverwaltungs-GmbH, a wholly owned subsidiary of Volkswagen Aktiengesellschaft (together, **Volkswagen**) (the **Acquisition**).

As a result of the Acquisition, Volkswagen's interest in the shares and voting rights of Everllence will be reduced from 100% to 49%, and Bain Capital and Volkswagen will together have the capacity to determine the financial and operating policies of Everllence, such that they will jointly control Everllence.

Bain Capital is a private investment firm with its registered office in Boston, USA, that invests in companies across a number of industries, including information technology, healthcare, retail and consumer products, communications, financial services and industrial/manufacturing.

Everllence, headquartered in Augsburg, Germany, is the parent company of the Everllence Group and operates globally through its subsidiaries as an engineering company specialising in propulsion and energy solutions for maritime, energy and industrial applications. Everllence develops and manufactures engines, turbomachinery and propulsion systems, with a focus on decarbonisation technologies and efficiency solutions. Everllence also provides lifecycle services including maintenance and performance optimisation through its global service network. Everllence has offices across Australia in Sydney, Perth and Melbourne.

Volkswagen is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange with its registered office in Wolfsburg, Germany, and is the parent company of the Volkswagen group (**Volkswagen Group**). The Volkswagen Group is active worldwide mainly in the development, manufacture, marketing and sale of passenger cars, light commercial vehicles, trucks, buses, coaches, chassis for buses and diesel engines, motor bikes, each including spare parts and accessories. The Volkswagen Group also engages in vehicle distribution, the development and marketing of mobility service solutions such as ride hailing and car sharing as well as financial and insurance services relating to the distribution and financing of its cars and commercial vehicles.

determination_table_content.details:
Funds managed and/or advised by Bain Capital Investors, LLC
(together, Bain Capital) propose to acquire 51% of the shares and
voting rights in Everllence SE (Everllence) and a number of its direct
and indirect subsidiaries (together, the Everllence Group) from
Volkswagen Vermögensverwaltungs-GmbH, a wholly owned
subsidiary of Volkswagen Aktiengesellschaft (together, Volkswagen)
(the Acquisition).
Bain Capital together with its wholly owned special purpose vehicle
Nikolaus (BC) Bidco GmbH (Nikolaus) applied for a notification
waiver in respect of the Acquisition.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Nikolaus, is a special purpose vehicle that is ultimately
controlled by Bain Capital. Bain Capital is a private investment firm
with its registered office in Boston, USA, that invests in companies
across a number of industries, including information technology,
healthcare, retail and consumer products, communications, financial
services and industrial/manufacturing.
The target, Everllence, headquartered in Augsburg, Germany, is the
parent company of the Everllence Group and operates globally
through its subsidiaries as an engineering company specialising in
propulsion and energy solutions for maritime, energy and industrial
applications. It develops and manufactures engines, turbomachinery
and propulsion systems, with a focus on decarbonisation
technologies and efficiency solutions. Everllence also provides
lifecycle services including maintenance and performance
optimisation through its global service network.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular, there is no horizontal overlap
or vertical relationship between Bain Capital (or its connected
entities) and Everllence in the supply of propulsion and energy
solutions for maritime, energy and industrial applications in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
